pivot_criterion.why: S5 (draft-head re-alignment) is a TRAINING job the autonomous loop cannot do. Kernel work and training compete for the same operator attention, so the loop must say plainly when kernel work has stopped paying rather than grinding sub-1% levers forever.
pivot_criterion.trigger: PIVOT when open_nontraining_levers == 0 on TWO consecutive audits, OR when three consecutive cycles adopt nothing >=1%. Either fires -> the auditor writes a PIVOT banner to FLYWHEEL_AUDIT.md and creates FLYWHEEL_PIVOT.

B8'' (~0.4%) and B1 (0.3-0.5%) are explicitly sub-1% and do NOT count. B8-cpasync is a different kernel and stays uncounted. S5 and S7 need training. B5 needs the no-additional-quantisation constraint relaxed. B9 is prefill, not decode. One more failure empties the kernel queue -- but the three-cycles-without-a-1%-adoption arm of the trigger has ALREADY fired this cycle, so the pivot is due now on that arm regardless.

position_at_definition.reading: The remaining kernel headroom is ~30% and is spread across many sub-1% items; the acceptance multiplier alone is worth 1.4x. When the kernel queue empties, the pivot is not a defeat -- it is the point where the larger lever becomes the only lever.
